test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 2 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.**
solution:
The correct answer is: **my**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'My'** is a possessive adjective and pronoun that we use where we already have a noun and want to indicate ownership.

 
 
• **Example -** *Those are **my__** glasses.*
 
 
 
• **'my'** is always placed before a noun.
 
• ​Here in the given paragraph,** 'my'** is used to explain that the glistering summer months belong to the speaker.
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate word is **'my'.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Correct Paragraph: ***While I was sitting there (1) **__sulking__** over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) **__my__** glistering summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally, she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **'Ours'** is used to referring to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker and one or more other people previously mentioned or easily identified.
 
• **'Me'** is used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• **'Mine'** is used in place of another noun when it's understood what's being discussed and adds information describing whose it is.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• Both **my** and **mine** are possessives, but they are used rather differently.
 
• **'My'** is put before a noun to indicate the speaker's possession.
 
 
• **Example -** *You have your talent. I have **my** talent.*
 
 
 
• **Mine** is similar to **my**, but it cannot be used with the following noun the same way as **my**, it can't be put before a noun.
 
• **'Mine'** is always used after a helping verb to refer to something previously mentioned.
 
 
• **Example -** *You have your talent. I have **mine**.*
